title: Article VIII of the Bylaws: Return of Retained Equity on the Board's Revolvement Cycle
content:
**Section 1.** Equity retained under Membership and Patronage Equity comes back to the member on the board's revolvement cycle and not on request.

**Section 2.** An allocation year becomes eligible once it has stood for the class's cycle in whole fiscal years, counted from the fiscal year the allocation was posted for, and the board then revolves that year's equity out of the annual pool in the order the class fixes.

**Section 3.** The pool is a percentage of unrevolved equity fixed each year by the board, so an eligible year is not necessarily paid in full in the first year it becomes eligible, and a member whose eligible year is only part paid carries the remainder into the next cycle.

**Section 4.** Revolvement is paid in the order the class fixes, which is ordinarily oldest allocation year first and, on the age retirement class, by the age of the member before the allocation year.

**Section 5.** Equity is never revolved below the class's minimum equity balance while the membership stays open.

**Section 6.** A member may not buy their way to the front of the cycle, offer a discount for early payment or ask the board to skip a year on hardship grounds; those are board decisions on which no standing policy exists.

## Reckoning eligibility

Eligibility is reckoned in whole fiscal years since the allocation year, so the count begins with the fiscal year the allocation was posted for and not with the year the board declared it or the year the member did the business.

**Boundary cases on hypothetical years.** On a class whose cycle is 12 fiscal years, an allocation posted for a fiscal year has stood 11 whole fiscal years at the close of the eleventh and is not yet eligible; at the close of the twelfth it has stood 12 and is eligible. On a class whose cycle is 15, the same allocation is not eligible until the fifteenth has closed.

**On part payment.** A year that becomes eligible and carries 3000.00 of credits is not necessarily paid 3000.00 in that year: the pool is what the board fixes, and whatever is not paid stays unrevolved and comes forward.

**On the floor.** A membership standing at 1100.00 of equity on a class whose floor is 1000.00 cannot be revolved by more than 100.00 while it stays open, since the floor is what keeps the class alive.
